name: Player
desc: Updates the player's position on the server. Has subclasses for different update types.

subclasses.name: C04PacketPlayerPosition
subclasses.desc: Position update (x, y, z) with onGround.

subclasses.name: C06PacketPlayerPosLook
subclasses.desc: Full position + rotation update with onGround.

fields.name: onGround
fields.desc: True if the player is on the ground

notes: S03PacketPlayer is the abstract base. C04/C05/C06 each have their own packet ID. The client sends C04 when only position changes, C05 when only rotation changes, and C06 when both change. onGround is ALWAYS present.

writeup.p: C03PacketPlayer is the abstract base of the serverbound movement family: four registered packet ids (0x03 bare, 0x04 position, 0x05 look, 0x06 pos+look) share one class with subclasses, and the vanilla client emits one of them every tick from EntityPlayerSP.onUpdateWalkingPlayer. The payload is a single onGround byte plus optional x/y/z doubles and yaw/pitch floats. Every server-side movement decision derives from it: position integration, ground state, fall distance, rotation, and the server's own movement validation. It is the most-sent packet in the play state and by far the most-abused one in the ten-client corpus.

NetHandlerPlayServer.processPlayer snapshots lastPos, computes the squared delta, and arms a hasMoved flag on the first small movement. Position values beyond +-3.0E7 on X or Z kick with "Illegal position". A reported Y of -999.0 disables the movement flag entirely (the client sends it when falling out of the world). The vanilla anti-cheat is the "moved too quickly" check: the sum of min(|delta|, |motion|) squared per axis must stay under 100.0, otherwise the player is teleported back with a warning. A residual delta over 0.0625 squared after moveEntity logs "moved wrongly" and snaps the player back. If the client reports onGround=false while the server thinks the player is grounded and Y is rising, the server calls jump(). Fall damage is applied from the server's own simulated fall state, which is what ground spoofing attacks.

The corpus splits into five families. Ground-state spoofers: NoFall in all eight clients, plus FastUse and Regen that send C03(true) or bare C03() to force the server-side regen tick. Movement engines: Flight (Nekoware, Rise 5.99, the 13+ mode Rise 6.x flight suite, Sigma, Spicy, Tenacity), Speed and Bhop (Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x, Sigma, Spicy), Step (Memeware, Nekoware, Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x, Sigma), Phase (Memeware, Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x NormalPhase, Sigma). Buffer and replay: Blink in Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x components, Sigma, Spicy and Tenacity. Position injection: Criticals offset ladders, TPAura and Infinite path walks, Damage utilities, AntiVoid, LongJump, and teleport modules. Disablers: Memeware, Rise 5.99, the Rise 6.x per-server suite, Sigma, Spicy and Tenacity all rewrite, cancel or re-inject C03 to break anti-cheat position timing. November Recode 2.0 contributes AntiVoid (watchdog C03 queueing), a rotation manager that rewrites the walking update, and a BlocksMC disabler; LiquidSense Dev contributes the HYT movement set, the Tp and Teleport lag-back walkers, Tower, Phase, ServerCrasher, FreeCam and LiquidWalk.

onGround is a single trusted bit that drives server-side jump physics and fall-damage accumulation: NoFall reports ground every tick so the server's entity never accrues fall distance. The 100.0 and 0.0625 squared-delta gates are the real vanilla anti-cheat, so every movement module must keep reported deltas under them or accept the teleport-back. The -999.0 Y sentinel is a free pass for vertical state: modules and commands use it to reset position without moving the player. Disablers weaponize the packet stream itself: cancelling C03 while Hypixel's watchdog is armed freezes the player server-side, and rewriting C06 into C04 (or the reverse) breaks anti-cheats that count packet-type ratios. Rotation is never validated against motion in vanilla, so spinbot and rotation-spoof modules can report any yaw/pitch.

implementation.overview: The movement spine of 1.8.9: one onGround byte plus optional position and rotation, emitted 20 times a second, trusted by the server for position integration, jump physics and fall damage. NoFall ground-spoofs it, Flight/Speed/Step/Phase forge its coordinates, Blink buffers it, Criticals and Damage inject offset ladders into it, and the disabler suites cancel or rewrite it to freeze the server-side player.
implementation.server_handling: processPlayer runs on the server thread and, for position-carrying variants, compares the packet position against the stored lastPos. The hasMoved gate requires the first reported movement to be under 0.25 squared before any validation starts. The "moved too quickly" check uses min(|delta|, |motion|) per axis, so large instantaneous deltas are masked by small motion values; the check teleports back via setPlayerLocation instead of kicking. "moved wrongly" fires when the post-integration residual exceeds 0.0625 squared and the player is not sleeping or in creative, also teleporting back. When the client reports onGround=false while the server-side player is grounded and Y is rising, the server calls jump(), which is the mechanism both criticals and the watchdog-disabler +0.16/+0.07 packet pairs exploit. The flight check runs when the player has no block collision under the bounding box and flight is disabled, kicking on sustained airborne motion.
implementation.protocol_notes: Four distinct ids map to one class: C03PacketPlayer (onGround only), C04PacketPlayerPosition (+x,y,z), C05PacketPlayerLook (+yaw,pitch), C06PacketPlayerPosLook (+both). The moving flag (field_149480_h) is set by the position constructors and the rotating flag by the look constructors; writePacketData emits the onGround byte first, then the doubles and floats conditionally. The -999.0 Y convention is a wire-level sentinel: the client sends C06 with y=-999 when falling out of the world, and the server clears the moving flag when it sees it. EntityPlayerSP selects the subclass by what changed this tick, and NetHandlerPlayClient answers S08 teleports with a C06 confirming the new position.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: NCP checks ground-state consistency (onGround true while falling), horizontal acceleration for speed, vertical acceleration for flight, and packet gaps for blink. Verus and AAC correlate rotation with motion, which is why Rise 6.x's PacketNoRotate rewrites C06 into C04 to strip rotations. Hypixel's watchdog is fought with the ground-truth +0.16/+0.07 jump-flag pair followed by full C03 cancellation for the watchdog window, disarmed by S08. Grim and Vulcan target packet-order and buffer abuse, countered by Rise 6.x modes like BufferAbuseFlight and the ConvertMovingPackets disabler. Timer-based flight and bhop (Spicy's 26.5 tps) flag timer checks unless the keepalive and transaction streams are delayed in lockstep, which is the disabler's second job.

modules.name: NoFall
modules.purpose: Eliminate fall damage by reporting onGround=true while falling, so the server-side entity never accumulates fall distance.
modules.how_it_works: Memeware's Hypixel mode fires C03(true) through sendPacketSilent (bus-bypassing) the moment fallDistance reaches 2 with ground below, then resets the local fallDistance; the Ground Spoof mode mutates the UpdateEvent ground flag so the vanilla emitter sends onGround=true in every packet while falling past 2.5 blocks. The two modes cover servers that do and do not validate extra packets.
modules.vanilla_hook: UpdateEvent; the injected C03(true) bypasses the packet event bus.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: NCP's ground check compares onGround against the simulated fall state; reporting ground mid-air is its classic flag, so packet-based NoFall is mostly caught by modern checks while ground-spoof variants that keep the arc believable last longer.
modules.variations: Nekoware sends C03(true) via sendPacketSilent on the same condition. Rise 5.99 sends C03(true) or a C06 with onGround true. Rise 6.x splits PacketNoFall (C03 true), FlagNoFall (C06 response spoof), PlaceNoFall, VulcanAndVerusNoFall and WatchdogNoFall. Sigma and Spicy send C03(true) on fallDistance thresholds; Tenacity's NoFallModule appears in the corpus via import only. LiquidSense Dev's NoFall ships the same onGround=true family (packet modes fire C03(true) on fall thresholds, SpoofGround/NoGround modes mutate the outgoing packet) plus an MLG mode that switches to a water bucket or web block with C09 and places it when a fall would miss the ground.

modules.name: Flight / Fly
modules.purpose: Move vertically and horizontally without the server's flight permission, by driving client physics and shaping the C03 stream the vanilla emitter sends.
modules.how_it_works: Nekoware's Vanilla mode sets motionY from input and horizontal speed directly and sends nothing, using a fall/ascend C04 pair every 700ms as anti-kick. Damage mode floods C0CPacketInput plus C03(true) each pre tick and starts with the fall-damage C04 ladder (y+3.05, y, y+0.41999998688697815) to gain the damage boost that defeats NCP flight checks. Verus mode places a C08 block below and zeroes motionY. The PacketOutEvent handler cancels C0F and C00 so the position stream is not correlated against transaction timing.
modules.vanilla_hook: UpdateEvent for physics, PacketOutEvent for the keepalive/transaction cancel, onEnable for the damage ladder.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The damage ladder leaves a fallDistance anomaly and requires taking fall damage at enable; the periodic anti-kick packets produce a Y sawtooth that NCP's flight check averages out over time. Cancelling C0F/C00 freezes ping and transaction state, which itself is a flag on transaction-aware servers.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99's Fly is a 2000+ line multi-mode module covering packet, ground, damage, S08-cancel and anti-cheat-specific variants. Rise 6.x ships 13+ named flight modes (AstralMC, BlockDrop, BufferAbuse, Creative, Funcraft, Grim, LatestNCP, MMC, MineLand, Vulcan, Watchdog). Sigma's Fly has multiple packet modes plus PremiumFlyAddon. Spicy's Fly mirrors BackupFly's 0.0624986421/0.0625/0.0000013579 C04 offset ladder. Tenacity's FlightModule sends C04 +0.3/+0.1 offsets and C03(false). LiquidSense Dev covers the family with the AquaVit HYT modules (HYTFly, HYTHighJump, HYTLongJump, HYTRun, HYTSpeed, Flight1, LastestHypixelFly, ShipGod, Stair) on top of the LiquidBounce-core Fly. The HYT modules cancel C03 subclasses and buffer them while airborne, LastestHypixelFly cancels C03 until an S08 arms the fly window, Stair climbs with C04 ladders, and ShipGod steers a ridden target with C04/C06 sends.

modules.name: Blink
modules.purpose: Freeze the server-side player by buffering every C03 (or every packet) and replaying the queue in order on disable, creating fake lag.
modules.how_it_works: On PacketSendEvent, with All Packets on, every outgoing packet is parked in a ConcurrentLinkedQueue and cancelled; with it off only C03PacketPlayer (and its subclasses) is held. Pulse mode flushes the queue every N ticks with a 10% random skip to bound the blink windows. onDisable replays everything with sendPacketWithoutEvent in FIFO order. An optional EntityOtherPlayerMP renders the frozen position to other players.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Any anti-cheat that measures the gap between movement packets flags long blinks; pulse mode bounds the gap and the random skip breaks periodicity. The flushed burst is also a tell, since the server sees a jump in position on release.
modules.variations: Rise 6.x moves this into BlinkComponent and MovementBlinkComponent (position-only) shared by Blink, BlinkAntiVoid and WatchdogAntiVoid. Sigma's Blink cancels C03 and C00 together on outgoing pre. Spicy's Blink cancels outgoing packets on its EventSendPacket. Tenacity's Blink event handles the C04/C05/C06 subclasses separately. LiquidSense Dev's Blink cancels C03 and the C04/C06/C08/C0A/C0B/C02 set into a LinkedBlockingQueue, renders a breadcrumb trail, spawns a fake player when pulse is off, and flushes via getNetworkManager().sendPacket on the pulse timer or on disable.

modules.name: Step
modules.purpose: Climb blocks higher than the vanilla 0.6 limit by reporting intermediate C04 positions that hide the vertical delta.
modules.how_it_works: Nekoware's NCP mode watches the ClimbSlabEvent; when the bounding box has risen past 0.6, it sends C04 at y+0.42 and y+0.75 with onGround false, then drops timerSpeed to 0.4 for two ticks so the faster climb does not trip horizontal speed checks. Vanilla mode just sets stepHeight locally. The 0.42/0.75 pair mirrors the NCP speed/bhop arc, which is why the module refuses to run while the client's Speed module is on.
modules.vanilla_hook: ClimbSlabEvent for the packet ladder; UpdateEvent for stepHeight and timer restore.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The server accepts the ladder because each reported position is within one tick's plausible delta; the timer slowdown hides the effective vertical speed. Checks that simulate stepping independently (Matrix, Vulcan) flag the 1.0-block rise regardless of the ladder.
modules.variations: Memeware's Step is the same packet ladder lineage. Rise 5.99 sends C04 at d plus random/2000. Rise 6.x splits NCPStep (d plus random/2000), NewNCPStep, MatrixStep (exact float ladder 0.41999998688698, 0.7531999805212, 1.00133597911215, 1.42133596599913, 1.75453595963335, 2.0026719582243), VulcanStep (single +0.5) and WatchdogStep (packet rewrite). Sigma sends first/second/off C04 ladders plus a C06 look variant.

modules.name: Speed / Bhop
modules.purpose: Move faster than vanilla sprint by manipulating jump arcs, timer speed and the movement packets the client emits.
modules.how_it_works: Spicy's Bhop Hypixel mode sets noClip, jumps on a 0.00004 ground check, and runs 26.5 tps plus random jitter in air so the vanilla C03 emission carries an accelerated trajectory. Test 3 mode drives EventMove directly: motionY 0.41999998688697815 on ground, speed seeded at forward*2.1500000953674316 and decayed by speed/165 per air tick, plus a random 1.0E-5..9.9E-4 Y jitter on ground packets. An S08 setback counter auto-disables after 3 lagbacks in 5 seconds.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventMove and EventMotion for physics; EventPacket on S08 for the lagback counter.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The 0.42 jump plus speed decay is the classic NCP bhop signature; the timer manipulation (26.5 tps) trips timer checks unless keepalive and transaction packets are delayed to match. The S08 auto-disable is an explicit flag-avoidance mechanism: the module quits before the anti-cheat can accumulate a ban.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99's Speed has NCP/LowHop-style modes that send C04 ground packets at specific moments. Rise 6.x ships FuncraftSpeed and InteractSpeed, which send C04 with onGround true on interact. Sigma's Bhop sends C04(x, -10, z, true) as a void trick, with PremiumBhopAddon extending it. LiquidSense Dev's HYTSpeed cancels C03 subclasses while active, and the core Speed module ships an S08 lagback check that rewrites yaw and pitch to the client rotation and zeroes motion on teleport.

modules.name: Disabler
modules.purpose: Break anti-cheat position timing by cancelling, rewriting or re-injecting C03 packets, usually paired with keepalive and transaction manipulation.
modules.how_it_works: Sigma's Hypixel mode arms a watchdog flag by sending C04 (x, y+0.16, z, true) and (x, y+0.07, z, true) through sendPacketNoEvent, then cancels every C03 in the outgoing pre phase until an S08PacketPlayerPosLook disarms it. ViperMC mode injects ten C04 packets alternating +-0.2 Y every 3 seconds. The keepalive and transaction branches (Erisium re-sends the last S00 key every 1500ms, SagePvP/ColdNetwork cancel accepted C0F with id 0) keep the frozen connection alive.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventPacket outgoing pre for C03 cancel and C04 injection; EventUpdate for the arming sequence.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The +0.16/+0.07 pair is the Hypixel watchdog jump-flag trigger, a ground-truth pattern the server accepts as a jump; the resulting 5 second free-move window is bounded by the watchdog itself. Cancelling C03 while armed freezes the server-side player, which is the point, and the S08 disarm prevents the freeze from persisting.
modules.variations: Memeware's Disabler has Mineplex Combat (C00 key corruption), Transaction, Latest Verus, PvPTemple, OmegaCraft, Timer, AACv1.9.10, Sloth, Ghostly, Watchdog and Faithful Movement modes. Rise 5.99's Disabler rewrites C06 into C04 and re-injects position packets. Rise 6.x ships ConvertMovingPackets, DynamicPVP, Ghostly, Lunar, NoRules, RiseBalance, Teleport, UniversoCraft and Verus2 disablers, most of which convert C03 subclasses or re-send position. Spicy has Disabler and Hypixel5SecDisabler (C04 +0.21/+0.11 pattern). Tenacity has DisablerModule and AdvancedDisablerModule with C06 to C04 conversion. November Recode 2.0's DisablerModule in BLOCKS_MC mode cancels the first outgoing C06PacketPlayerPosLook after join (before tick 120) and corrupts every C0FPacketConfirmTransaction uid to Short.MAX_VALUE; WATCHDOG mode is a TODO stub.

modules.name: AntiVoid
modules.purpose: Rescue the falling player by shaping the C03 stream before the server's void kill: SETBACK raises the reported Y, WATCHDOG cancels and buffers C03 over the void.
modules.how_it_works: EventWalkingUpdate PRE raises the walking-update Y by +1 (SETBACK), snaps Y to a 1/64 modulus with onGround forced true (VULCAN), or calls jump() (JUMP). WATCHDOG cancels every C03 while aboveVoid() and fallDistance > 0.1, parks the packets in a ConcurrentLinkedQueue, and flushes the whole queue plus a bare C03 once 120 packets accumulate.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The WATCHDOG buffer bounds the freeze window at 120 packets, so the server never sees a long movement gap; the SETBACK and VULCAN modes send no extra packets at all and only change what the vanilla C03 reports, which keeps them invisible to packet-rate checks.
modules.variations: Only November Recode 2.0 in the corpus; Rise and Spicy AntiVoid variants use the S08 teleport as their trigger instead (see S08PacketPlayerPosLook).

modules.name: RotationManager
modules.purpose: Central rotation spoofing service: track the server's rotation from outgoing C03 packets and inject module-chosen yaw and pitch into the walking update the vanilla emitter turns into the next C03.
modules.how_it_works: On EventPacket.Out, a rotating C03 stores its yaw and pitch as the server rotation. On EventWalkingUpdate PRE, the spoofed angles overwrite the event yaw and pitch plus the render rotations for keepTicks ticks; MoveCorrection.BASIC and FREE re-apply the yaw on EventStrafe so movement direction follows the spoof. Modules request rotations through spoof(priority, keepTicks, angles) and the highest priority wins.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Because the server rotation is learned from the client's own C03 stream, spoofed look stays consistent with what the server last recorded for the player, which is what rotation checks compare against.
modules.variations: LiquidSense Dev tracks rotations in RotationUtils and OtherRotationUtils, which rewrite C03 yaw, pitch and position directly inside PacketEvent instead of using a management singleton.

modules.name: Teleport / Tp
modules.purpose: Teleport by spoofing C04 position streams instead of moving: packet sequences toward a target BlockPos, with the server's own lag-back used as the arm signal.
modules.how_it_works: onEnable provokes a lag-back with C0F(0,-1,false), a flying-abilities C13 and C04 +0.17/+0.06, then every C03 is cancelled until an S08 flips tp=true. The tick handler then replays the fall ladder (0.060100000351667404, 5.000000237487257E-4, 0.004999999888241291 + 6.01000003516674E-8) and walks a PathfindingUtils path with per-vec3 C04s, finishing with C03(true) and C0C input. The core Teleport module adds per-AC modes: Blink and Flag wrap the C04 burst in STOP/START_SNEAKING, Spoof rewrites C03 x/y/z to the target, AAC3.5.0 cancels and queues C04/C06.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketEvent (C03 cancel and mutate), onEnable send burst, TickEvent for the path walk.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The C04 stream keeps every reported position inside one tick's plausible delta, which is what defeats naive teleport checks; the lag-back arming means the server confirms the start position before the module moves.
modules.variations: Tp.java (AquaVit) is the lag-back-armed variant that walks a computed path; TeleportCommand reuses the +0.41999998688697815/+0.675319998688697815 C06 pair and rewrites S08 rotation after teleporting.

modules.name: Phase
modules.purpose: Walk through solid blocks by sending C04 position bursts into the wall and cancelling the vanilla push-out.
modules.how_it_works: While collided horizontally and on ground, Vanilla and Spartan modes send the six-packet C04 shuffle (self, 0.5/0/0.5, self, self + y + 0.2, 0.5/0/0.5, self + 0.5) and nudge the client position along the yaw; Skip sends +0.06 ladders with directional offsets. AAC3.5.0 mutates C03 x and z by 1e-8 along the movement direction, and onPushOut cancels the push-out so the block never ejects the player.
modules.vanilla_hook: UpdateEvent (ladder sends), PacketEvent (C03 mutation), PushOutEvent (cancel), MoveEvent (Mineplex mode).
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The position bursts are sub-tick moves, so the server's moved-too-quickly gate never trips; the cancelled push-out is the part modern anti-cheats flag, which is why the per-AC modes exist.
modules.variations: November's PhaseModule is a different animal: it phases through cage glass by deleting the block client-side and cancelling all packets while the window is open (see S08PacketPlayerPosLook).

modules.name: ServerCrasher
modules.purpose: Crash or lag the server by flooding C04 positions with absurd coordinates.
modules.how_it_works: AACNew floods 9999 C04 packets at pos + 9412*index per axis in one onEnable burst; AACOther uses 500000*index; AACOld sends a single C04 at NEGATIVE_INFINITY. MassiveChunkLoading walks C04 from the player Y to 255 in 5-block steps plus a 6685-packet diagonal sweep; CubeCraft alternates +0.09999999999999 and ground C04 pairs 3000 times per motion tick.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Trips packet-rate limits and server-side position validation immediately on any protected server; this is a grief tool, not a bypass. Tenacity's Crasher floods C0A swings instead of C04 (see C0APacketAnimation), the same intent on a cheaper packet.
modules.variations: None in the corpus for this packet; the only other flood-style module is Tenacity's Crasher.

modules.name: Tower
modules.purpose: Rise one block per jump by placing beneath and sending C04 height ladders; the C03 involvement is the packet-mode fake jump.
modules.how_it_works: Packet mode, on ground with a 2-tick timer, sends C04 +0.42 and +0.753 then snaps the client position up one block; other modes (Motion, MotionTP, Teleport, AAC3.3.9) drive motionY or setPositionAndUpdate. Auto-block switches to the block slot with C09, places through onPlayerRightClick, and swings via swingItem() or a C0A packet when swing is off.
modules.vanilla_hook: MotionEvent for the ladder, onPlayerRightClick for the placement.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The +0.42/+0.753 pair mirrors the NCP jump arc, which keeps the vertical delta inside one tick's plausible range; the 1-block rise is what simulation-based checks (Matrix, Vulcan) flag.
modules.variations: None in the corpus for this packet; November's ScaffoldModule tower modes fold the same motion into its placement loop.

modules.name: FreeCam
modules.purpose: Detach the camera: cancel every C03 and C0B so the server never sees the ghost movement, leaving a fake player at the original spot.
modules.how_it_works: On enable, spawns EntityOtherPlayerMP (-1000) cloned from the player and sets noClip. PacketEvent cancels C03PacketPlayer and C0BPacketEntityAction; UpdateEvent flies with motion and strafe. On disable, snaps back to the stored position and removes the fake player.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Cancelling the movement stream while airborne reads as a blink window, which is a flag on its own; the fake player at the origin keeps the server-side entity frozen in place.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 Freecam cancels C03 as part of its packet passthrough list; LiquidSense FreeCam additionally cancels C0B.

modules.name: LiquidWalk
modules.purpose: Walk on liquids by mutating the C03 Y with a sub-pixel offset so the server keeps the player on the surface.
modules.how_it_works: In NCP mode, when the bounding-box bottom is inside a liquid, toggle nextTick and subtract 0.001 from packetPlayer.y on alternate ticks; the vanilla emitter keeps running, so the stream stays continuous while the reported Y fights the sink.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: A 0.001 Y offset is far below the 0.0625 residual threshold, so the server never logs a wrong-move; the tell is the alternating pattern if an anti-cheat integrates vertical deltas over time.
modules.variations: None in the corpus for this packet; other clients implement surface walking through their speed and fly modules instead.

implementation.general_hooks: Every client intercepts C03 at the outgoing packet event (PacketOutEvent, PacketSendEvent, EventSendPacket) and matches instanceof C03PacketPlayer, which also catches the C04/C05/C06 subclasses. Movement engines hook UpdateEvent or PreMotionEvent to alter position, ground and rotation before the vanilla emitter builds the packet; Rise 6.x additionally routes through TeleportEvent for S08 responses.
implementation.client_variations: Vanilla emission differs per client: Memeware and Nekoware patch EntityPlayerSP.onUpdateWalkingPlayer to fire a custom UpdateEvent that carries setY/setGround, Sigma and Spicy do the same with their motion events, while Rise 5.99 and Tenacity rewrite the emitter to consume their own event objects. Send paths diverge the same way: sendQueue.addToSendQueue (Memeware, Nekoware, Sigma, Spicy, Tenacity), PacketUtil.sendPacket and sendPacketWithoutEvent (Rise 5.99), PacketUtil.send and sendNoEvent (Rise 6.x). Bus-bypassing sends (sendPacketSilent, sendPacketNoEvent, sendPacketWithoutEvent, sendNoEvent) are universal and used whenever a module must not re-trigger its own packet listener.

anticheat.overview: The position packet family (flying, position, position-look, look) is the heart of every movement anticheat: it is the only stream that tells the server where the player is. All 50 cloned anticheats key their motion checks off it. The corpus splits into classic statistical checks (Frequency FlyA, Arc NoFall, Hydro GroundA) that score deltas against expected physics, and modern simulation checks (Grim PredictionRunner, Photon MovementSimulator) that predict the next position from client inputs and flag the residual. Ground-spoofing, fly, speed, phase, step, timer and blink are all detected from this one packet family.

checks.name: MovingFlying adapter (NoCheatPlus)
checks.purpose: The classic 1.8 ProtocolLib adapter that feeds every C03 variant into NCP's moving checks.
checks.how_it_works: Wraps PacketPlayInFlying, PacketPlayInPosition, PacketPlayInPositionLook and PacketPlayInLook through ProtocolLib, builds a MovingData context (position, rotation, ground flag, exact move vector), and dispatches to the full moving check set: survivalfly, morepackets (timer), noswing, nofall, and the passable/phase checks. Handles 1.7-1.8 protocol differences and the -999 teleport sentinel.
checks.detects: Fly, speed, timer, nofall, phase/clip, blink, and every movement-based cheat that alters the position stream.
checks.variations: Frequency and Degrade use WrappedPlayInFlying on their own event bus; CloudAC ships WrapperPlayClientFlying; CheaterDeleter hooks PlayerMoveC2SPacket via a Fabric mixin.

checks.name: FlyA (Frequency)
checks.purpose: Classic 1.8 fly check: vertical motion must match gravity and jump physics.
checks.how_it_works: PostCheck on WrappedPlayInFlying: tracks the y delta and ground flag, compares against expected gravity, jump momentum and piston/water modifiers, accumulates a buffer and fails on persistent impossible vertical motion. Small, event-driven, representative of the 1.8 generation.
checks.detects: Fly modules, vertical speed, highjump, and any vertical motion that ignores gravity.
checks.variations: Azure Fly, Hydro FlightA, FlopAC FlightA/B, Truthful BFlyA and MC-Jinky FlightFCheck are the same statistical pattern on different bases.

checks.name: NoFall (Arc v2)
checks.purpose: Ground-spoof check: onGround=true while the fall distance says the player is airborne.
checks.how_it_works: On the flying packet, reads the ground flag and the accumulated fall distance; if the player reports onGround while their vertical velocity and fall distance are inconsistent with landing, the check fails. Directly targets the C03 onGround spoof used by nofall modules.
checks.variations: Grim NoFall (groundspoof package) predicts landing from the simulation; Hydro GroundA compares the ground flag to collision results.

checks.name: GroundA (Hydro)
checks.purpose: Ground-flag consistency check against server-side collision state.
checks.how_it_works: On each position packet, compares the client's onGround flag with the server's own collision check at the reported position; a mismatch between the flag and the block below is a ground-spoof flag. 20-line check, the minimal form of the ground consistency idea.
checks.detects: NoFall and ground spoofing where onGround does not match the terrain.
checks.variations: Negativity NegativityPlayerMoveEvent runs the same comparison on Bukkit's PlayerMoveEvent instead of raw packets.
